name: Bar Chart
hint: Switch Grouped → Stacked: the bars slide together and climb onto each other.
description: Grouped, stacked and 100% bar chart for comparing categories across one or a few series: your rows, your series, your formats. The layout morphs instead of re-rendering: grouped bars slide together and climb into stacks with a 2px surface gap, 100% stretches them to full height while the axis re-labels to percentages, and sorting reorders categories with FLIP springs. Negative values hang from the zero baseline. Hovering lifts a bar and dims its siblings; the glass tooltip shows value and share, or the full breakdown and total in stacked modes. Arrow keys move between bars, the legend hides series without repainting the rest, values label only where they fit, and narrow containers flip to horizontal ranking bars. The sample content (`demo`) is a year of profit for six bike shops.
intents: stacked bar chart with percent toggle
sales by store per quarter chart
animated bar chart that switches grouped and stacked
usage: Use to compare a handful of categories (3 to 12) across 1 to 8 series that share one unit. Pass `data` (rows of plain objects), `xKey` (the category field) and `series: [{ key, label, tone }]` (or `yKey` for one series); format with `formatValue` (tooltip, table, hero), `formatAxis` (ticks) and `formatLabel` (labels on bars). Own the data states with `loading`, `error` + `onRetry` and `emptyMessage`; `onPointClick({ category, series, value, row })` fires on click or Enter. Pick grouped to compare series within a category, stacked for totals, 100% for mix; `sort` is "total", "alpha" or "none" (your row order; the older object shape always sorts by total). Keep one value axis; for a trend over many periods use Area Chart. The in-card switches are the kit's shared `Segmented` control from components/_shared/chart.jsx, which has no slug of its own. The older { title, subtitle, note, series, categories, values } object still works as `data`.

dataProps.description: Rows of plain objects, one per category: the category under `xKey` (and an optional stable `id`), one number per series under its key. Missing values count as 0. The older { title, subtitle, note, series: [{ id, label, long }], categories: [{ id, label, short }], values: { [id]: number[] } } object is still accepted.
Field holding each row's category label.
Shortcut for one series: the field holding its value. Ignored when `series` is given.

[{ key, label, long, tone }]: the value fields, in group / stack order. `long` adds a longer name to legend and tooltip; `tone` is a series slot 0–7 or a --ts-* token name. Series keep a fixed order in every group and stack, so position tells them apart as well as colour.
Card title (also the accessible name when a string).
Line under the title.
Footnote under the plot.
(value, series) => string for tooltip, table, hero and summary. Default: Intl number in the Theme's locale, minus sign, no unit.
(value) => string for value-axis ticks. Default: compact Intl number.
(value) => string for the labels drawn on or beside bars. Default: formatAxis.
Header of the category column in the table view.
Accessible name of the legend.

Label of the total row in the stacked tooltip and of the table's total column.
true shows the total of what is visible above the plot; a node replaces it with your own.

("total" | "alpha") => void from the in-card switch. `sort` sets it from outside.
("vertical" | "horizontal") => void from the in-card switch. `orientation` sets it from outside.

Show the sample: six bike shops' quarterly profit in dollars, with its titles, note and copy. Your own props win over it.

example:
<BarChart
  data={regions}          // [{ id: "emea", name: "EMEA", q1: 120, q2: -14 }, …]
  xKey="name"
  series={[{ key: "q1", label: "Q1" }, { key: "q2", label: "Q2" }]}
  title="Margin by region"
  formatValue={(v) => new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "EUR" }).format(v)}
  loading={isFetching}
  error={error?.message}
  onRetry={refetch}
  onPointClick={({ row }) => openRegion(row.id)}
/>
